claims.quote: I think we can do better by turning the stack element into a standalone class that is either a prevector or a `std::shared_ptr<std::vector>` depending on the element's size.
claims.request: turn the stack element into a standalone class that is either a prevector or a shared_ptr depending on element size

status_by.quote: Is that worth the complexity in consensus-critical code though?

claims.status_note: author explored how the struct could be laid out and committed to investigate whether a union type improves push performance

claims.author: Yudis-bit
claims.harm: static elemTrue introduces cross-core atomic contention on the shared_ptr control block in CCheckQueue during parallel script verification
claims.quote: Wait, doesn't `elemTrue` introduce cross-core atomic contention in `CCheckQueue`?

status_by.quote: Moving them to locals eliminates the bus lock bouncing, but replaces it with two unconditional heap allocations on every

claims.status_note: author moved them to execution locals, but Yudis-bit countered that this causes two unconditional heap allocations on every EvalScript call; author replied arguing benchmark allocates locals once per

claims.author: Yudis-bit
claims.harm: wrapping stack elements in std::shared_ptr doubles heap allocations and adds unnecessary atomic refcounting on the thread-local interpreter hot path
claims.quote: wrapping elements in `std::shared_ptr` doubles heap allocations on the hot path

status_by.quote: The interpreter hot path shouldn't pay heap or refcounting overhead for a non-existent attack. Concept NACK.

claims.status_note: author argued benchmark regressions were limited to VerifyNestedIfScript, but reviewer reiterated allocator churn and gave a Concept NACK

claims.author: Yudis-bit
claims.harm: penalizing existing script evaluation with heap and refcounting overhead mitigates an attack that is consensus-invalid today and should be budgeted by future soft forks
claims.quote: The 10KB duplication attack is consensus-invalid today under `MAX_SCRIPT_ELEMENT_SIZE = 520`. Any future soft fork that raises element limits must budget its own hashing costs anyway

status_by.quote: We did consider enforcing new consensus rules as a solution... However, we reasoned that additional implementation complexity (pointers and caching) was worth it for a simpler and more permissive consensus rule set

claims.status_note: author explained they preferred implementation complexity over arbitrary consensus limits or budget discontinuities

claims.author: Yudis-bit
claims.harm: pointer identity does not imply data equality, so pushing identical elements separately bypasses a pointer-keyed cache while pinning dropped elements in memory
claims.quote: pointer identity does not imply data equality. Pushing identical elements separately creates distinct allocations, bypassing a pointer-keyed cache entirely while pinning dropped elements in memory.

status_by.quote: I don't think we need be concerned with attacks that push identical elements, because such pushes must be paid for by the attacker in bandwidth and fees.

claims.status_note: author explained identical pushes are bounded by bandwidth/fees and cache only needs to prevent cheap duplicate-and-hash asymmetry

claims.author: ismaelsadeeq
claims.quote: Another potential direction is to have the (proposed sigop) opcode read from multiple stack elements instead of one.
claims.request: stream signatures across multiple <=520-byte stack elements instead of raising the element size limit, avoiding the large-element attack surface altogether

status_by.quote: We did consider this type of chunking as an option. Ultimately this would be a trade-off that passes complexity down to wallet developers and users.

claims.status_note: author explained chunking pushes complexity onto wallet developers and users, especially for variable-size signatures
